_comment: Endpoint presets. Each entry is both a per-endpoint quirk table for the OpenAI-compatible client (matched by base_url) and a starting point the dashboard offers when adding an endpoint: picking one fills in the URL, the protocol and the key variable, and carries the quirks the endpoint needs. An endpoint with no entry here gets the portable default: bare model name, no extra headers, no reasoning remap. Add or override entries with MIRA_PROVIDERS_JSON_PATH.

_fields.label: Display name, shown on the Connections page and under each model picker.
_fields.description: One sentence for the card and the preset list.
_fields.docs_url: Where the provider documents its API and plans.
_fields._naming: An entry's key is what `llm.provider` names it by, so it may not be 'openai' or 'bedrock': those two have always meant the generic OpenAI-compatible backend and AWS Bedrock, and an entry taking either name would be unreachable from the config file. OpenAI's own API is therefore 'openai-api'.
_fields.base_url: The endpoint this profile applies to; `llm.base_url` is matched against it, and the dashboard prefills it. `llm.provider: <name>` fills it in too.
_fields.api_key_env: Environment variable holding the key when one is not stored in Mira's database. "" means the endpoint needs no key.
_fields.api_style: Protocol dialect the endpoint is reached with: 'chat' (Chat Completions) or 'responses'.
_fields.model_prefix: 'keep' sends the full vendor/model id (OpenRouter routes on it); 'strip' sends the bare model name.
_fields.extra_headers: Headers added to every request (attribution, client identification).
_fields.reasoning_effort_map: Renames for the unified reasoning.effort levels this endpoint spells differently.
_fields.reasoning_param: How a Chat Completions request asks for a reasoning level: 'reasoning_effort' (the OpenAI field, what OpenAI-compatible endpoints take) or 'reasoning' (OpenRouter's nested {effort} object). The Responses API always uses the nested form.
_fields.models_dev: This endpoint's provider id on models.dev, whose per-model reasoning_options say which levels each model takes. The picker offers those levels and a requested one is snapped to the nearest the model has. Empty for an endpoint the catalogue does not list.
_fields.session_header: Optional header carrying a stable per-conversation id (one per client instance, so one per review pass), for endpoints that route and cache by it.
_fields.usage_url: Optional GET endpoint reporting the key's allowance. Its document is read by the parser named in usage_format.
_fields.usage_format: Which parser reads usage_url's document (see mira.llm.key_providers). Currently: 'opencode-go'; or 'ledger' for a subscription with no usage API, whose meters Mira estimates from the tokens it recorded spending (see plans).
_fields.plans: With usage_format 'ledger': the subscription's plans, keyed by the id an endpoint's `plan` setting names. Each has a label and its metered windows: {minutes, credits, anchored}. `credits` is the window's allowance in plan credits (USD of usage value times the model's credit_multiplier in models.json); `anchored` windows restart every `minutes` from the subscription's start date when one is configured, and roll otherwise.
_fields.plan_reference_models: With plans: models whose remaining allowance the card restates as USD of that model's usage (credits left divided by its credit_multiplier), for subscriptions that document their limits per model.
_fields.stream: true to read Chat Completions replies as server-sent events, so a reply still arriving is judged by llm.stream_idle_timeout rather than killed at llm.request_timeout. Off for an endpoint not known to stream tool calls.
_fields.echo_reasoning: true to send an assistant turn's reasoning_content back with the next request of a tool loop, which DeepSeek's thinking mode requires. A 400 naming the field turns it off for that model.

openrouter.label: OpenRouter
openrouter.description: Pay-per-token access to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek and more behind one key.

opencode-go.label: OpenCode Go
opencode-go.description: OpenCode's $10/month subscription to open coding models (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and more), metered in 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows.

open-design.label: OpenDesign Cloud
open-design.description: OpenDesign's coding-plan subscription to DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude, GPT and more behind one key, metered in plan credits over 5-hour and 7-day windows.

plans._comment: Allowances in plan credits, derived from the per-model limits OpenDesign's billing page lists: Go is $55 of Eco (x0.27) or $30 of Flash (x0.5) per 7 days, both 15 credits, and $18 / $10 per 5 hours, both 5 credits; Plus is $74 / $40, 20 credits. Pro and Max list $90 and $150 of Flash per 7 days.

opencode-zen.label: OpenCode Zen
opencode-zen.description: OpenCode's pay-per-token catalogue — Claude, GPT, Gemini and the open models — on the same key as Go.

openai-api.label: OpenAI
openai-api.description: OpenAI's own API, billed to your OpenAI account.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
deepseek.description: DeepSeek's own API, direct and cheap for its own models.

groq.label: Groq
groq.description: Open models served fast on Groq's own hardware.

together.label: Together AI
together.description: Hosted open models, pay per token.

fireworks.label: Fireworks AI
fireworks.description: Hosted open models with function calling, pay per token.

ollama.label: Ollama
ollama.description: Models running on your own machine or network. No key needed; point the URL at the host running Ollama.
